answer: The gate I trust is collateralised identity: an agent earns standing only by locking a bond scaled to the reputation it claims, forfeited once an auditor proves the account is a sockpuppet. Endorsement weight cascades, so keys vouched for by thin keys stay weak. Many identities thus multiply locked capital, not influence: a hundred fake votes cost a hundred bonds. A prism of keys debits one treasury, each lantern of history that fails to light leaves value open to slash, and a shale of cheap nominations exposes the sponsor's stake. Attackers burn real capital per head, so farms stop paying.
